summary.headline: HPCL swung to INR9,822 crore EBITDA in Q2 FY27 from a INR14,860 crore loss in Q1, with PBT of INR6,768 crore and standalone GRM of $32.15/bbl pre-SAED.
summary.overview: HPCL reported a sharp recovery in Q2 FY27, with EBITDA of INR9,822 crore against a Q1 loss of INR14,860 crore, and PBT of INR6,768 crore versus a Q1 loss of INR17,446 crore. Management credited stronger refining and marketing physicals, July-August crude inventory gains (described as small), and cost and capex control, while noting September crude cycle turned against them. Standalone PAT was INR3,438 crore and consolidated PAT INR3,625 crore, with standalone leverage at 1.38 (from 1.52). The Rajasthan (HRRL) refinery reached about 60% utilisation, with a debt refinancing cutting rates by about 105 bps, and management expects PBT-positive operations in October. Management declined to give specific guidance on LPG compensation, Vizag RUF stabilisation timing beyond March, or refinery-wise margins.

segments.name: Refining (standalone)
segments.commentary: Q2 GRM $32.15/bbl pre-SAED, described by management as significantly above Q1; strong physical refining and sales performance cited as main driver.

segments.name: Marketing
segments.commentary: Marketing margins described as decent versus significant under-recovery in Q1; non-fuel activity now at about 10% of pan-India outlets, up from 5.5% at start of year. Navya LPG launched with a target of about 1 lakh primary sales by Diwali.

segments.name: Rajasthan refinery (HRRL)
segments.commentary: Running at about 60% utilisation since September; Q2 GRM about $12/bbl with October first-half GRM around $16 post-SAED, and $60 cited as current-month gross figure. Management expects October PBT-positive and revenue above INR4,000 crore in October; 400+ TMT to be shipped in October.

segments.name: Vizag RUF (residue upgrade)
segments.commentary: Running at 60-70% capacity; uplift currently about $0.6-1.0/bbl (October expected $0.65-0.7, about INR500 crore GRM), versus a $2-3 target not yet achieved.

segments.name: Chhara LNG terminal
segments.commentary: Terminal working about 10 months a year; 5-6 cargoes expected in H2 for about 15-20% utilisation; management expects terminal plus gas buying to be cash positive for FY27.

segments.name: Renewables and CBG
segments.commentary: 275 MW wind and solar operating, 270 MW solar plus BESS under construction, 500 MW under development, all captive. 5 of about 10-11 GOBARdhan CBG plants under construction.

guidance_outlook: Rajasthan refinery: full run rate of 8-8.5 MMTPA expected after high-sulphur crude switch in December, with one remaining unit to be commissioned around Diwali plus about a month; full steam by end of Q3, subject to timing of a week or two. Management said GRMs on high-sulphur crude could be $20-plus in Q4.
Vizag RUF: management is holding to full uplift guidance, hoping for stabilisation by March or earlier, but not ruling out April; next quarter expected to show higher utilisation and GRM impact.
Petchem at Rajasthan: cracker expected to start around Q4 FY27; petchem benefits, barring propylene, not expected in FY27.

HRRL debt refinancing: about 105 bps lower rate, annual interest benefit INR470-500 crore from October 3; a further INR1,000 crore interest reduction cited after equity conversion. State interest-free loan of about INR1,100 crore per year, first tranche INR375 crore received.
Standalone leverage: management wants to bring debt-equity from 2:1 down after cash flow visibility; no debt repayment projection given yet, to be updated next quarter.
capex_capacity: Rajasthan (HRRL) CDU running at about 55-60% utilisation since September; secondary units nearly all on hot sink, with VGO-HDT expected on hot sink imminently and one more unit before Diwali, followed by sulphur recovery unit completion.

Rajasthan equity: Government of Rajasthan infused INR1,500 crore in Q2; HPCL converted about INR4,300 crore subordinated loans to equity; HPCL has about INR300-400 crore balance left against a project cost of about INR79,800 crore.
Vizag RUF running at 60-70% of capacity, with the licensor still stabilising the first unit of its technology globally.
Renewables: 275 MW operating, 270 MW under construction, 500 MW under development, all for captive use; line of sight to 1 GW+ over two years.
EV charging: 5,500-odd retail chargers; weekly charging revenue up 3x since start of year (small base).
demand_pricing: Crude sourcing described as highly volatile; buying increasingly on landed/DAP basis, with freight costs nearly doubling Q1 to Q2 (Suezmax from about $4/bbl to $9/bbl).
Crude processed lags procurement by about 30-35 days for West Coast and about 45 days for East Coast; HRRL longer due to pipeline transfer.
Brent at about $114 on the call date; management said diesel and product cracks likely to hold through winter months but declined to forecast.

Standalone sourcing cost per barrel fell by about $30-40 between Q1 and Q2 per analyst; management attributed this to lower-priced opening inventory marked-to-market at June end and strong July-August.
LPG under-recoveries: management did not give extension details on government compensation; buffer balance INR18,049 crore receivable from government.

qa_highlights.question: What is the effective crude sourcing premium over Brent, and how did LPG under-recoveries and Q3 margins trend?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to quantify premiums, calling crude sourcing 'Wild West' with same-cargo prices moving $10/bbl in days. LPG under-recovery was INR245/cylinder in October and INR327/cylinder in November; Q2 total under-recovery about INR500 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Is the government LPG compensation being extended beyond the current period, and what is the Vizag RUF uplift timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to discuss government dialogue. RUF uplift currently about $0.6-1.0/bbl, about 40-50% of expected benefit; full benefit guided by March or possibly April, with stabilisation described as a 'doubles or quits' challenge.

qa_highlights.question: Did HRRL debt refinancing involve corporate guarantees, and what changed in terms?
qa_highlights.answer: Terms largely the same with the same consortium; 3 new bankers added and project finance converted to operating. No corporate guarantees given.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q2 sourcing cost per barrel fall sharply, and what drove GRM of $27.89?
qa_highlights.answer: Partly lower-priced opening inventory marked to market at June end, benefiting July; strong July-August and operational optimisation. September was weaker as crude cycle turned.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Rajasthan GRM and when will product be self-sufficient?
qa_highlights.answer: October first-15-day GRM about $16.1 post-SAED; expected 20-plus after high-sulphur switch in December. Management said HRRL product will be absorbed by HPCL, with about 95% of requirement met internally once Barmer and JVs run.

qa_highlights.question: What is the HRRL net debt and capital structure target?
qa_highlights.answer: Management has not yet projected net debt; debt repayment and debt-equity reduction from 2:1 to be addressed next quarter after cash flow visibility.

risks_watch: Crude volatility and freight spikes: landed-cost premiums and freight nearly doubled Q1 to Q2; September showed margin reversal when crude cycle turned.
LPG under-recovery rising from INR245 to INR327 per cylinder (Oct to Nov); unclear extension of government compensation beyond the current period.
Vizag RUF utilisation and GRM uplift still below the $2-3 target; stabilisation timing has slipped repeatedly.
Rajasthan ramp-up: full 8-8.5 MMTPA run rate depends on sulphur recovery unit commissioning and high-sulphur crude switch in December; petchem not before Q4 and benefits from FY28.
Standalone leverage of 1.38 remains above management's comfort level; equity infusions and debt repayment plan still to be quantified.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on the operational turnaround, particularly Rajasthan and the Q2 numbers, but cautious on crude costs, LPG compensation and RUF stabilisation timing. Management repeatedly declined to give numbers on government dialogue, refinery-wise margins and HRRL net debt projections.

growth.why: Management guides HRRL to 8-8.5 MMTPA run rate by end Q3 FY27 (about 60% utilisation now) with GRMs of $20-plus post-December, backed by a timeline on the unit commissioning and crude switch, but no revenue growth percentage was given; Vizag RUF uplift remains below its $2-3 target and LPG compensation and refinery-wise margins were not guided.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Q2 GRM $32.15/bbl pre-SAED and Rajasthan GRM guided to $20-plus post-December, with Vizag RUF uplift of $0.65-0.7/bbl (about INR500 crore GRM) in October, though September crude cycle turned against them and Brent near $114 keeps crude-cost risk high.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.when: Q3 FY27 (full steam by end Q3)
rows.why: HRRL at about 60% utilisation with one remaining unit due around Diwali plus a month and full 8-8.5 MMTPA run rate by end Q3; 270 MW solar plus BESS under construction and cracker start around Q4 FY27.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Rajasthan refinery ramping from about 60% utilisation toward an 8-8.5 MMTPA run rate by end Q3, with 400+ TMT shipped in October and revenue above INR4,000 crore guided for October.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Management expects further equity calls in the next 1-2 quarters on HRRL (about INR300-400 crore left against INR79,800 crore project cost), and renewables line of sight to 1 GW+ over two years, but no new capex was announced.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management is upbeat on the Q2 swing and HRRL GRM of $16 in early October rising to $20-plus post-December, but gave no formal guidance raise and the September margin reversal tempers this.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Vizag RUF uplift is only $0.6-1.0/bbl against a $2-3 target with stabilisation slipping from March to possibly April, LPG under-recovery rising from INR245 to INR327 per cylinder, and standalone leverage at 1.38.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Rajasthan petchem cracker expected to start around Q4 FY27, and Navya LPG launched with a target of about 1 lakh primary sales by Diwali.

rows.label: Standalone debt-equity from 1.38 toward 2:1 target
rows.why: Standalone leverage fell from 1.52 to 1.38, HRRL debt refinancing cuts rates by about 105 bps (INR470-500 crore annual interest benefit from October 3), but no debt repayment projection has been given yet.

rows.label: Samridhi benefit run-rate INR600-700 crore
rows.why: Samridhi benefit of INR327 crore (about $0.18/bbl) accrued in Q2 with run-rate locked in at about INR600-700 crore.

rows.label: LPG government compensation extension
rows.why: LPG under-recovery of INR245/cylinder in October rising to INR327 in November, with INR18,049 crore buffer receivable from government, but management declined to discuss extension.

tone.note: Management was confident on the Q2 operational turnaround and Rajasthan ramp-up, but cautious on crude sourcing volatility, LPG compensation, and Vizag RUF stabilisation timing; analysts pressed on LPG extension, RUF timeline and HRRL net debt, which management largely declined to quantify.
